profile.name: Muhammed Fasal
profile.headline: Cybersecurity Researcher · VAPT & Web Application Security
profile.short_bio: Focused on vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, web application security, and security research—with hands-on experience identifying, validating, documenting, and helping remediate security weaknesses.
profile.long_bio:
I am an early-career cybersecurity professional with a primary focus on vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, and web application security. My work combines structured testing with manual validation, risk-focused reporting, and remediation guidance.

Through internship experience, security projects, labs, and bug bounty research, I have worked with OWASP Top 10 testing, application mapping, authentication and authorization checks, and common security tooling. I also bring hands-on IT administration exposure, which strengthens my understanding of the systems and people security work must support.

projects.title: Hospital Management System Security Assessment
projects.short_description: Structured security assessment of a PHP-based Hospital Management System in an authorized, controlled testing environment.
projects.description: Authorized testing of a local, intentionally vulnerable PHP application—not a production hospital system.
projects.problem: A PHP-based Hospital Management System needed an independent review of authentication, authorization and input handling before it could be treated as trustworthy.
projects.solution: Mapped application areas, reviewed authentication, authorization and input handling, then manually validated observations using Burp Suite and browser tools. Findings were organized against OWASP guidance and prioritised with risk assessment.
projects.methodology: Application mapping → authentication and authorization review → input handling review → manual validation → risk classification → structured reporting.
projects.testing_methodology: OWASP Top 10 based manual testing with Burp Suite and browser tooling.
projects.findings_summary: Produced a structured assessment format covering evidence, impact, remediation recommendations, and reporting. Findings are not listed publicly because only documented, sanitized results should be shared.
projects.remediation_summary: Findings were paired with prioritised remediation guidance and verification steps.

projects.title: WebSafeScan
projects.short_description: Bash-based utility for initial web security checks: headers, TLS configuration, cookie attributes, and technology fingerprinting.
projects.description: Automate repeatable early-stage web security checks without replacing manual penetration testing.
projects.problem: Early-stage web security checks are repetitive and easy to skip, which weakens the coverage of an assessment.
projects.solution: Checks HTTP security headers, TLS and certificate configuration, cookie security attributes, and technologies exposed by a target. The tool combines Bash with Curl, OpenSSL, SSLScan, and WhatWeb.
projects.methodology: Repeatable automated checks produce consistent coverage; results are then reviewed in context before being treated as findings.
projects.testing_methodology: Automated header, TLS and cookie checks with manual review.
projects.findings_summary: Automation is useful for coverage and consistency; results still require contextual review and manual validation before they are treated as security findings.

projects.title: Custom Linux Privilege Escalation Lab
projects.short_description: A self-created CTF machine for learning Linux enumeration, insecure configuration review, and privilege-escalation concepts safely.
projects.description: Self-created Linux CTF lab, designed exclusively for controlled learning.
projects.problem: Privilege-escalation concepts are hard to learn safely without a controlled, reproducible environment.
projects.solution: Practice methodical enumeration and identify insecure Linux configurations that can create a privilege-escalation path.

projects.testing_methodology: Manual Linux enumeration and privilege-escalation testing in a self-controlled lab.
projects.findings_summary: The lab explores permissions, sudo configuration, SUID binaries, capabilities, cron jobs, and service configuration, with defensive remediation considered alongside each concept.

writeups.title: Building a repeatable web security baseline check
writeups.summary: How WebSafeScan turns repetitive header, TLS and cookie checks into a consistent baseline — and why the output still needs a human.
writeups.content:
## Context

Early assessment work is repetitive: the same header checks, the same TLS review, the same cookie attributes. Repetition is exactly where coverage gets skipped.

## Approach

WebSafeScan automates that baseline: HTTP security headers, TLS and certificate configuration, cookie security attributes, and the technologies a target exposes.

## What it does not do

Automation produces coverage, not conclusions. Every result still needs contextual review and manual validation before it is treated as a finding.

## Takeaway

Automate the boring 20% so the manual 80% gets the attention it deserves.
